In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hipparco results for the nearer stars, in the distance range 100-300 pc, are not in conflict with any other results, and are consistent with the Hipparcos trigonometric parallaxes.
the Hipparos results on the distances of the nearer stars should be taken as a working hypothesis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Hipparos based luminosity calibration of nearby stars appears to be reliable for stars of spectral type F and earlier, but that for stars later than about F0 there is a systematic error of about +0.1 mag in the absolute magnitudes derived from the Hipparcos distances.

the luminosity calibration based on the Hipparcos distances is in good agreement with the calibration based on main sequence fitting, with the exception that the calibration of the Hyades is about 0.1 magnitude too bright.

the distances to the nearest OB associations are well established, that the distances to nearby open clusters are probably reliable, that the Hipparcs distances to the more distant open clusters are uncertain, but that the uncertainties do not exceed a factor 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hipparos distances to the nearest OB associations and open star clusters are reliable.
Hipparcos distances to open clusters are in good agreement with main sequence fitting distances.
the Hipparcs results on distances to OB associations and open cluster are in good agreement with the results from main sequence fitting and that the luminosity calibration is not in serious trouble.
